issues.title: Desktop: validate Wails WebView compatibility and finalize the shell decision
issues.context: FOUNDATION work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: A.T.O.M is qualified primarily in Chromium. Native WebKit, current Vite routing, durable browser storage, navigation enforcement and HTML/PDF printing are not qualified. Selecting a shell without those checks risks a product fork.
scope: Build a disposable proof of concept around the current React/Vite frontend and real Go API on WKWebView and WebKitGTK; compare against a fixed Chromium baseline.
Start with pinned stable Wails v2 (current documentation v2.17.0). Record exact versions; v3 is beta and is not an automatic workaround.
Exercise development HMR and release-like assets, stable application origin/profile, relative JSON/Blob HTTP routes and cancellation, native print feasibility and navigation/bridge isolation.
Publish the findings, measured costs, declared OS/architecture matrix and accepted architecture decision. Switch to Electron with the same sidecar if the gate fails.
acceptance_criteria: Both native targets cover startup, Leaflet/tiles, markers/rays/polygons, canvas/SVG, themes, Results, Pareto, drawers and keyboard focus, plus Run Sector, 8-Cell evaluation/optimization and existing 4G/5G/6G availability.

Project workspace, run history and retained report bytes survive relaunch and a changed sidecar port; report HTML/PDF is readable with complete quantities/lineage and native Open/Save is demonstrated.
PASS requires all critical flows and navigation/auth/storage/print checks, HMR p95 <=1s over 20 warmed edits, supported APIs, and no product or framework fork.
ACCEPTABLE WITH FIXES allows at most three bounded presentation/accessibility defects totaling <=3 engineer-days, with regression scope, closed and rerun before accepting Gate 2.

SWITCH TO ELECTRON on an unresolved critical failure on either OS, Vite downgrade/fork requirement, unsafe navigation, lost storage, unusable print/PDF, or HMR >2s after one bounded investigation. Do not maintain separate shells per OS.
Record OS/hardware/toolchain/engine/commit/pack hashes, native automation feasibility, startup/memory/package estimates, and framework choice. Playwright WebKit alone does not satisfy this gate.
non_goals: No production shell rollout, broad native UI, RF changes, API-to-binding migration, Vite/React upgrade, full installer pipeline or release claim.

contributor_notes.effort: M: approximately 3-5 engineer-days, plus native test access
contributor_notes.risk: High: framework and platform compatibility blocker
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: establish the thin shell and shared platform capability adapter
issues.context: FOUNDATION work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: There is no native delivery entry point. Copying screens or moving Go domain calls into bindings would create independent web and desktop products.
scope: Create a desktop/ host module using the shell accepted by D01; keep native dependencies out of backend-go headless builds.
Point shell configuration at ../frontend-react and stage existing dist assets only as build output. Add one small src/platform capability interface with browser/native adapters.

Provide one resizable normal window, icon/title/About/VERSION, Quit, safe external-link dispatch, standard menu/keyboard hooks and bounded remembered geometry. Native file actions are completed in later issues.
Wire injectable host/process/dialog interfaces for focused tests; use no duplicate RF/report/persistence logic.
acceptance_criteria: The current React screen launches in an unsigned local native build from the shared source; browser builds require no native runtime.
RF/API calls remain on the shared HTTP boundary. Native bindings/preload expose only typed host capabilities, not a generic filesystem or execution API.
Closing the only window quits instead of hiding a background backend; About reports the canonical product version and build identity.
No committed duplicate frontend, dist source tree, API types, domain serializer or RF implementation is added.
non_goals: No new product navigation, tray, agent, global shortcut, multi-window system, file association or native UI rewrite.

contributor_notes.risk: Medium: shell boundaries and build coupling
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: supervise the bundled Go backend on a dynamic loopback endpoint
issues.context: FOUNDATION work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: The Go server assumes environment/cwd paths and a default fixed port, publishes no actual ephemeral endpoint, and has no desktop parent-death or crash supervision. /readyz also assumes on-disk frontend assets.
scope: Bundle the existing Go server as a child binary and add only opt-in desktop startup/control support; retain the current web/API entry point.
Have the child bind 127.0.0.1:0 once and announce its actual endpoint/PID/protocol/build/readiness over private inherited control pipes. Construct absolute resource paths and a curated environment.
Implement startup/readiness/failure states, expected-process identity checks, bounded startup timeout, child crash monitoring, explicit recovery and per-user single-instance focus behavior.
Implement parent-EOF shutdown, cancellation/drain/reaping and bounded forced termination of only the owned child; capture minimal startup stderr immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent unrelated uses of 8080 do not affect desktop launch; no free-port probe/rebind race, LAN bind, public endpoint file or zombie child occurs.
Readiness distinguishes listener, dataset and UI. A clean Vite-only workspace works without stale dist output; public Docker/web /readyz semantics remain intact.
Missing/mismatched binary or pack, startup timeout, child crash, repeated launch, normal quit and abrupt host death have deterministic tested outcomes.
Requests/jobs cancel or drain under existing limits; shutdown uses a bounded ceiling (existing 30s maximum) and reaps the child. RF work is never silently replayed.
Restart rotates the runtime generation and rejects late results from the prior child without overwriting newer project/result state.
non_goals: No in-process RF rewrite, generic process manager, automatic RF retry, fixed 8080 dependency or changes to RF limits.

contributor_notes.risk: High: cancellation, orphan prevention and state safety
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: secure stable-origin API routing and native capabilities
issues.context: FOUNDATION work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: Loopback is reachable by other local users and webpages. Current web CORS and optional API keys do not authenticate the complete desktop surface, and serving UI from a random port would change IndexedDB origin.
scope: Implement the D01-proven stable application origin and allowlisted asset/API router; the host privately discovers and updates the dynamic sidecar target.

Generate a 256-bit random token per child generation, deliver it through a private pipe and inject it only in the host/server-side dev proxy. Cover all desktop API/status/meta paths, including JSON and Blob calls.
Validate Host/exact Origin where present, preserve auth even when Origin is absent, restrict proxy paths and destinations, apply production CSP to host-served HTML and isolate dev HMR permissions.

Enforce native top-level/new-window/redirect/drag navigation restrictions, safe external HTTPS links, permission denial, and typed dialog-approved file capabilities. Isolate report HTML from the main native bridge.
acceptance_criteria: Foreign webpages, wrong/missing tokens, other-user clients, rebinding Host values, unexpected origins, invalid proxy destinations and prior-generation requests fail without credentials or project leakage.
Credentials never enter URL, argv, VITE variables, renderer storage, logs or public temp files. CORS is not treated as authorization.
All actual-engine navigation vectors and imported/stored HTML tests demonstrate that untrusted content cannot invoke native authority; click interception alone is insufficient.
Production CSP permits required local/Wails/Leaflet behavior and approved tiles without broad unsafe script or wildcard network allowances. Dev-only WebSocket access is absent from release.
Browser/Docker/API semantics remain supported; coordinate with existing open PR #63 without changing or merging it in this work.
non_goals: No account system, TLS/PKI for private loopback, public API exposure, arbitrary file/exec binding or framework security fork.

contributor_notes.risk: High: local authorization and privileged WebView boundary
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: preserve Vite HMR and safe Go rebuilds in the development loop
issues.context: FOUNDATION work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: Current Vite proxies hard-code localhost:8080, and Wails shell watching alone will not supervise rebuilds of a separately bundled sibling Go server. Full installer builds would destroy iteration speed.
scope: Add proposed scripts/desktop-dev.sh, desktop-build.sh and desktop-test.sh with clear dev/local-build/package modes; keep current web/Docker commands.
Use the existing frontend directory and the D01-proven Vite external dev server/API proxy/HMR configuration, all desktop dev listeners on loopback with server-only credentials.

Watch backend-go/raytracer and compile the replacement sidecar before swapping; reconnect through the stable host route and runtime generation. Watch shell sources separately for Wails rebuild/relaunch.
Document prerequisite setup, first build versus warm edits, failed-compilation recovery, isolated dev profiles and command cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: 20 representative warmed JSX/CSS edits have edit-to-visible p95 <=1s with no Go rebuild or package generation.
A small Go backend edit rebuilds/reconnects within the initial <=5s warm guidance; a shell edit within <=10s; actual measurements and reference hardware are recorded.
Failed Go compilation preserves the last good child, successful replacement cancels stale work safely, and Ctrl-C/relaunch leaves no extra processes.
A clean clone can run desktop dev without existing dist, signing credentials, DMG/AppImage/deb production or a second React app.
Existing npm/Vitest/Playwright and Go commands, browser Vite development and docker compose up --build -d atom remain usable independently.
non_goals: No mandatory root Makefile, frontend major upgrade, installer-per-edit workflow or new product transport.

contributor_notes.risk: Medium: HMR routing and process restart coordination
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: use native data directories and durable WebView storage
issues.context: MVP work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: Current data discovery depends on cwd/container layout, and projects/history/report bytes use separate origin-scoped browser stores. Ephemeral origins, profile resets or cache cleanup could lose desktop work.
scope: Resolve native per-user data/config/cache/log/state/runtime paths; use macOS Application Support/Caches/Logs and Linux XDG defaults with private permissions.
Configure and verify a durable release WebView profile/stable origin for all current stores; isolate dev/test profiles and preserve store/domain schemas.
Add a small settings/dataset-registry/recent-file association store without replacing domain persistence. Treat installed bundles as read-only.
Handle missing/unwritable paths, interrupted settings writes, disk/quota failure and version upgrades with explicit recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Workspace, run history and artifact bytes survive relaunch, sidecar port changes, application relocation and a tested upgrade using the existing IndexedDB/repository contracts.
Changing/clearing cache does not clear durable projects, reports, packs or the release profile. Browser data is never silently migrated or reset.
Relative XDG overrides are ignored; private Unix dirs/files have 0700/0600 access; Unicode/space paths and failed writes are covered.
Project/report files chosen by users stay in their chosen destinations; autosave is identified as recovery, not a portable file save.
No writes use cwd, repository paths, /app or the installed app bundle, and headless behavior remains available.
non_goals: No SQLite migration, second project database, cloud synchronization or schema change.

contributor_notes.risk: High: durable data and upgrade behavior
contributor_notes.platform_relevance: macOS 14+ arm64/x86_64 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64; validate proposed support in the spike

issues.title: Desktop: integrate validated dataset packs and production map access
issues.context: MVP work package in the A.T.O.M desktop roadmap. Desktop is another delivery target for the existing React/Go product; macOS and supported Linux come first, Windows later. Audited VERSION 0.12.3, HEAD b22b0937e8295d25587f7157368a70ec58a71077. This issue is planned work, not evidence that the capability exists.
issues.problem: Dataset discovery assumes configured directories/Docker resources, has no user-folder registry/install flow, and production basemap access differs from localhost development. The default manifest flags redistribution terms needing review.
scope: Add Data -> Add Dataset Pack via directory or manifest selection; reuse complete LoadDatasetPack validation and display identity/source/license/size/hash information.
Offer managed copy by default and advanced reference-in-place; stage/validate/atomically register copied declared files and store approved referenced roots in a native registry.
Preserve validated runtime switch and project dataset ID/version/hash semantics; handle duplicate identity/content, moved/unmounted references, permission/disk failures and cancellation.

Record a maintainer-approved redistribution basis for the existing default pack, or select an already-supported approved sample/default pack. Include it as read-only bundle data without a required first-run download.
Resolve actual desktop Stadia authentication or a policy-compliant visible OSM fallback, attribution, application identification, normal caching and offline tile-error behavior.
acceptance_criteria: No terminal, environment edit or Docker volume is required to add/activate/reopen a pack; selected pack persists across app restarts.
Bad layer/manifest hashes, traversal/symlink escapes, incomplete copies, ambiguous duplicate IDs and changed reference contents are rejected without changing the active pack.
Copied packs are revalidated at staging/activation; references revalidate on load. External source files are not mutated or deleted.
Clean-machine planning works with approved bundled data; package size accounts for the current ~111 MiB building data. Redistribution/provenance evidence is recorded before public distribution.
Production tile requests work under a documented provider arrangement without spoofing localhost or embedding a private shared key; denied/offline tiles retain RF overlays and useful error handling.
No offline-area prefetch is added. OSM/Stadia policy and credential redaction are checked against current official documentation.
non_goals: No arbitrary-city ingestion, new dataset archive/format, weakened integrity rules, RF model changes or offline basemap distribution.

contributor_notes.effort: L: approximately 4-7 engineer-days plus external provider/data decisions
contributor_notes.risk: High: dataset integrity, redistribution and network dependency blocker

issues.title: Desktop: package macOS app bundles and architecture-specific artifacts

issues.problem: The repository ships containers, not a self-contained native macOS app. A development-machine launch does not establish installability, resource layout or Intel/Apple Silicon support.
scope: Build .app bundles for the spike-approved macOS floor (proposal macOS 14+) with separate arm64 and x86_64 artifacts.
